# 24 hr. Pet Emergencies

Illness and injuries can happen unexpectedly at any hour of the day or night.  When your pet requires immediate veterinary attention and your pet’s regular veterinarian is not available.   JEFFERSON ANIMAL HOSPTIAL is always open and fully staffed for emergencies as well as routine care, any time of the day or night- seven days a week, 365 days a year.

## Our veterinarians and trained staff are on the premises ready for you 24 hours a day!

Image: dividerImage: divider

## EMERGENCY SERVICES:

Our hospitalized patients receive around-the-clock monitoring and intensive care.

We are fully equipped for emergency treatment, laboratory tests, emergency and routine surgery, ultrasound and endoscopy,  radiology,  chemotherapy,  dentistry and intensive care.

Our support staff is well-trained in emergency triage and supportive care. 

There may also be times when your regular veterinarian is treating your pet and wishes to refer your pet to our facility for overnight or prolonged critical care monitoring. We work closely with your regular veterinarian, providing regular medical updates at their request. We also provide your regular veterinarian with complete medical treatment records, giving them the appropriate tools to successfully manage follow-up care for your pet.

## If your pet needs veterinary care please call us

### (502) 900-PETS

### Accredited by AAHA

We have been AAHA Accredited for over 40 years.  We set our standards high so that we can provide you and your pet(s) the highest quality of veterinary care possible.

### Open since 1978

We are celebrating our 45th year of providing 24/7 veterinary care to the pets of Louisville, Kentucky and Ohio. Read more about our history.

Jefferson Animal Hospital

4504 Outer Loop
Louisville, KY 40219

+1 (502) 900-PETS

## Specialty Care by Appointment at VSP Louisville

VSP is home to the largest veterinary cancer center in Kentucky, offering medical oncology and chemotherapy for dogs and cats. We are also the only provider of I-131 radioactive iodine therapy for hyperthyroid cats in Kentucky, and the only practice in the state that treats hyperparathyroidism in dogs with ethanol ablation.

Our specialty team covers internal medicine, cardiology, neurology, surgery, interventional radiology and urinary stone management, and we offer hyperbaric oxygen therapy. VSP was the first of three practices in the United States to get a thulium laser. Advanced imaging, including CT, fluoroscopy, ultrasound and digital radiographs, helps us find answers here instead of sending you somewhere else.

You don’t need a referral to book a specialty visit, although we’re always glad to work with your family veterinarian and keep them in the loop.

## Areas We Serve

We’re a short drive for families in Middletown, Anchorage, Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Lyndon, Prospect, Douglass Hills and Eastwood, and for anyone along the Shelbyville Road corridor in eastern Louisville. Pet owners also come to us from across Kentucky and Southern Indiana, especially for specialty care like I-131 therapy and cancer treatment.

## Directions to 11600 Main St

VSP Louisville is at 11600 Main St, Louisville, KY 40243, in the heart of Middletown, one block south of Shelbyville Road near Harrison Avenue.

From Interstate 265 (Gene Snyder Freeway), take Exit 27 for Shelbyville Road (US 60) and head west into Middletown. From Interstate 64, take Exit 15 for Hurstbourne Parkway toward Middletown, follow it north to Shelbyville Road, and head east into Middletown, or stay on Interstate 64 to Interstate 265 north and use Exit 27. From Southern Indiana, cross the Lewis and Clark Bridge on Interstate 265 and continue south to Exit 27. From St. Matthews, Shelbyville Road east takes you straight into Middletown.

For turn by turn directions, open our location in Google Maps.

Get Directions

## Parking and Arriving

Park in our lot. If your pet can’t walk, is too heavy to carry or you just need a hand, call us from the car at (502) 901-7990 and a team member will come out to help bring your pet in. Once you’re inside, let the front desk know you’ve arrived or that you checked in online. Please keep dogs on a short leash and cats in a carrier, since there may be other nervous pets in the lobby.

# Veterinary Oncology and Chemotherapy in Louisville

At Veterinary Specialist Partners (VSP) in Louisville, we provide compassionate and advanced cancer care for dogs and cats. Our veterinary oncology team uses detailed diagnostics, chemotherapy, surgery, and targeted treatment options to create a personalized care plan for each patient. From diagnosis through ongoing treatment, we support pets and their families with clear guidance, comfort focused care, and hope at every stage.

## Advanced Oncology
Care for Pets

Expert Pet Cancer Care, Every Step of the Way

The VSP team specializes in diagnosing and treating cancer in dogs, cats, and other pets. Using advanced diagnostics like cytology, biopsies, and state-of-the-art imaging (CT scans, digital radiographs, and ultrasound), we can identify cancer early and create personalized treatment plans. Our goal is to provide compassionate, expert care while using innovative therapies such as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and minimally invasive procedures for improved outcomes and comfort.

At Veterinary Specialist Partners (VSP),  our canine oncology team provides advanced cancer care customized to each dog’s diagnosis and treatment needs. Services may include tumor removal surgery, chemotherapy for cancers affecting the body, and minimally invasive procedures such as urethral stenting and transurethral resection of bladder tumors. Our team guides pet parents through every stage of care with clear information, personalized treatment, and compassionate support.

### Services include:

  * Advanced imaging (CT, Ultrasound) for staging and planning
  * Cytology and biopsy for accurate cancer diagnosis
  * Chemotherapy protocols personalized to your pet’s needs
  * Pain management and palliative care for comfort and quality of life

Image

## Personalized Oncology Plans for Every Pet

Every cancer case is unique, so our team creates custom treatment plans to meet your pet’s needs. From monitoring benign tumors to treating aggressive cancers, we focus on comfort and the best possible outcomes.

### Our veterinary cancer treatments include:

Surgery, Chemotherapy & Immunotherapy – Pets often tolerate chemotherapy well, with 85% experiencing minimal side effects.

Interventional Therapies – Minimally invasive options like urethral/ureteral stenting and TURBT for urinary cancers.

Cryosurgery (Freezing) – Effective for certain tumor types with less invasiveness.

At VSP, we combine expertise and compassion to guide you through every step of your pet’s cancer journey.

## When to See a Veterinary Cancer Specialist

Some signs of cancer in pets can be subtle, while others require urgent attention. Our veterinary oncologists are trained to evaluate these concerns and guide families through the next steps with clarity and care. If you notice any of the following symptoms, your pet should be evaluated as soon as possible:

  * Abdominal swelling
  * Bleeding from the mouth, nose, or other body openings
  * Difficulty breathing or eating
  * Lumps, bumps, or discolored skin
  * Non-healing wounds
  * Persistent diarrhea or vomiting

VSP is headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, providing emergency, urgent, and specialty veterinary care to pets throughout Louisville and its surrounding towns. We also operate Veterinary Specialist Partners (VSP) Evansville in Indiana, where we currently offer internal medicine, oncology, cardiology and medical neurology by appointment, with emergency and urgent care opening in early December 2026.

VSP in Evansville, Indiana, offers internal medicine, oncology, cardiology and medical neurology by appointment, with emergency and urgent care opening in early December 2026. We are also headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, where we provide emergency, urgent, and specialty veterinary care to pets throughout Louisville and its surrounding neighborhoods.

###### Advanced Specialty Care

###### Chemotherapy & Radiation (Oncology)

Available

We offer chemotherapy and radiation therapy as part of our oncology services to treat cancer in pets, aiming to control the disease and improve quality of life. Our oncology team works closely with you to develop a tailored treatment plan based on the specific cancer type and your pet's overall health. We utilize advanced protocols to target cancer cells while minimizing side effects.

###### CT Scan & MRI (Advanced Imaging)

Available

We provide advanced imaging services including CT scans and MRIs to obtain detailed pictures of your pet's internal structures for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. These sophisticated imaging techniques allow us to visualize complex anatomical structures and detect conditions that may not be visible with standard X-rays or ultrasounds. We work with specialized radiologists to ensure the highest quality imaging and interpretation.

###### Dialysis (Advanced Kidney Care)

Available

We offer dialysis as an advanced treatment for pets with severe kidney failure to help remove waste products and excess fluid from the blood when the kidneys can no longer function effectively. This therapy can significantly improve a pet's quality of life and slow the progression of kidney disease. We provide dialysis in a dedicated facility with experienced staff to ensure the safety and comfort of our patients.

###### Stem Cell Therapy (Regenerative Medicine)

Available

We offer stem cell therapy as a regenerative medicine approach to treat conditions such as osteoarthritis and tissue injuries in pets by utilizing the body's own repair mechanisms. This innovative therapy involves harvesting, processing, and reinjecting a pet's own stem cells to promote healing and reduce inflammation. We are excited to offer this cutting-edge treatment option to our patients.

Mr. Jones presented a question to the board regarding 201 KAR 16:010 Section 13 regarding the board’s 
code of ethical conduct and the reporting of disciplinary actions by a veterinarian to the board. Mr. 
Jones received a question from an attorney representing an unidentified veterinarian.  The attorney 
questioned the use of the words “and” vs “or” in this section. The attorney asked if the board required 
reporting of voluntary surrender only if there was also a conviction of a crime, since the word “and” is 
present in the regulation.  Mr. Jones’ opinion is that the word “and” is not appropriate because voluntary 
surrender and conviction of a crime must both be reported, even if the other is absent.  After review and 
discussion the board agreed. Mr. Jones advised the board to have this changed in their regulations. No 
further action was required
